LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.1: Whole Numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Whole Numbers, part of Numbers in Grade 5 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Where can we use ordering of numbers in real life? 2. 2. Why should we round off numbers?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of thousands in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read and write numbers up to tens of thousands in words in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. order numbers up to tens of thousands in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. round off numbers up to tens of thousands to the nearest hundred and thousand in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. apply divisibility tests of 2, 5 and 10 in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of thousands in different situations,

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read and write numbers up to tens of thousands in words in different situations,

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. order numbers up to tens of thousands in different situations,

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. round off numbers up to tens of thousands to the nearest hundred and thousand in different situations,

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. apply divisibility tests of 2, 5 and 10 in real-life situations,

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify place value of digits up to hundreds of thousands using place value apparatus or place value charts,

2. identify total value of digits up to hundreds of thousands using place value charts,

3. read numbers up to hundreds of thousands in symbols from number charts or cards,

4. read and write numbers up to tens of thousands in words from number charts or cards,

5. arrange numbers up to tens of thousands in increasing and decreasing order,

6. discuss and round off numbers up to tens of thousands to the nearest hundred and thousand using number cards and share with other groups, 1. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify place value of digits up to hundreds of thousands using place value apparatus or place value charts,
2. identify total value of digits up to hundreds of thousands using place value charts,
3. read numbers up to hundreds of thousands in symbols from number charts or cards,
4. read and write numbers up to tens of thousands in words from number charts or cards,
5. arrange numbers up to tens of thousands in increasing and decreasing order,
6. discuss and round off numbers up to tens of thousands to the nearest hundred and thousand using number cards and share with other groups, 1. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Whole Numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Link to other learning areas:

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of thousands in different situations,
2. read and write numbers up to tens of thousands in words in different situations,
3. order numbers up to tens of thousands in different situations,
4. round off numbers up to tens of thousands to the nearest hundred and thousand in different situations,
5. apply divisibility tests of 2, 5 and 10 in real-life situations,

Remember the key question: Where can we use ordering of numbers in real life? 2. 2. Why should we round off numbers?
